description:
Fetch one verse whole: the Sanskrit in Devanāgarī and IAST, the word-by-word breakdown with the meaning each word carries in this passage, the literary translation, the commentary, and optionally the surrounding verses.

Call it after search_texts when you are going to quote, and whenever the user names a verse. The word-by-word table is what lets you explain or re-translate a line honestly instead of trusting a finished translation.

Accepts citations as people write them, not only internal ids.

To read a chapter or a whole book in order, use browse_work. To read on around one verse, call this again with `context` 5 and then with the `unit_id` of the last neighbour marked "after"; each reply carries the five verses on either side with their translations.

context.description: Verses to include either side, within the same chapter. Use 1–2 when the argument depends on what surrounds the verse. Default 0.

language.description: Preferred language of the translations returned. Not a filter: works that exist only in Russian are returned in Russian, and each result says which language it is actually in. Default: en.

verse.description: A citation — "BG 2.47", "Бхагавад-гита 2.47", "Mahabharata 1.1.1", "Upanishads Mundaka 2.2.8" — or a `unit_id` from an earlier result.

name: get_verse
title: Read one verse in full
